label: prf:confinement-sdp
title: Proof of confinement sdp
html:
Proof. Proof of confinement sdp

Proof (sketch)

The program is a semidefinite program over the symmetric cone \mathbb{S}_+^N, N = \dim_R H_n(R, q), and existence/attainment of the optimum is standard convex duality.

  1. The feasible set is a compact spectrahedron and the objective is bounded below. The normalisation \mathrm{tr}(\Phi) = n_{\mathrm{target}} together with \Phi \succeq 0 confines \Phi to a bounded slice of the PSD cone, on which the linear objective \langle T, \Phi\rangle attains its minimum \Phi^\star \succeq 0.

  2. Slater \Rightarrow strong duality. Under the strict-feasibility hypothesis (ctx.slaterStrictFeasible: a \Phi_0 \succ 0 strictly satisfying every per-block and 2\times2 pair constraint, available at generic q where |q + q^{-1}| > 0), the conic-duality theorem gives strong duality — the dual SDP is solvable, \mathrm{primal} = \mathrm{dual}, and the complementary-slackness identity \Phi^\star(y_0^\star I + \sum_\lambda y_\lambda^\star \pi_\lambda - T) = 0 certifies optimality ([boyd-vandenberghe-2004], §5.9). The shadow prices y_\lambda^\star \ge 0 are exactly the per-block Frobenius-positivity duals of the LP/SDP witness contract.

  3. The scalar LP is the diagonal restriction. When every Wedderburn block decouples (no off-diagonal pair constraint binds), the matrix SDP collapses block-by-block to the confinement LP, with equal primal/dual values.

The Lean sibling encodes the data as ConfinementSDPData and states confinement_sdp conditional on slaterStrictFeasible; the conic-duality step is deferred there via sorry (-- Ref: [manuscript]), pending a Mathlib SDP strong-duality API. \square
